sources.author: Harrison Chase
sources.headline: Co-founder & CEO @ LangChain
sources.post_summary: Discussed the rapid evolution of AI agents from simple chains to autonomous multi-step systems. Highlighted how LangGraph enables developers to build reliable agent workflows with stateful orchestration and human-in-the-loop controls.

sources.author: Dmitry Shapiro
sources.headline: Founder & CTO @ Adept
sources.post_summary: Shared insights on scaling AI infrastructure for agentic workflows. Covered challenges in memory management, tool use reliability, and cost optimization when deploying agents at enterprise scale.

sources.author: Santiago Valdarrama
sources.headline: AI Engineer & Educator
sources.post_summary: Posted a technical breakdown of building production-ready AI agents using open-source frameworks. Emphasized the importance of evaluation frameworks, observability, and fallback mechanisms for reliable automation.

sources.author: Kelvin Liew
sources.headline: Head of Developer Relations @ Replit
sources.post_summary: Explored how AI coding agents are transforming developer workflows. Shared real examples of agents handling debugging, code generation, and deployment automation within Replit's environment.

sources.author: Elena Voss
sources.headline: Head of GTM Engineering @ Ramp | Ex-Salesforce
sources.post_summary: Discussed building a GTM engineering function that owns outbound infrastructure end-to-end. Shared how her team reduced manual prospecting by 65% by combining intent data, enrichment, and automated sequencing into a single owned platform.

sources.author: Marcus Hale
sources.headline: VP Revenue Operations @ Notion
sources.post_summary: Explained how his RevOps team restructured content strategy around buyer journeys instead of product features. The shift led to a 3x increase in SQL conversion by aligning blog, email nurture, and sales enablement content to specific pain points.

sources.author: Priya Sharma
sources.headline: Founder & CEO @ OutboundOS
sources.post_summary: Shared lessons from automating 40k+ personalized cold emails per month. Key insight: treating outbound like product engineering with version control, A/B testing infrastructure, and rollback capabilities dramatically improved reply rates while staying compliant.

sources.author: David Kwon
sources.headline: Director of Sales Operations @ Rippling
sources.post_summary: Detailed how his team built an internal 'GTM data lake' that unifies CRM, intent signals, and content performance. This enabled precise attribution of which content pieces actually influenced pipeline, changing how marketing and sales collaborated on content.

sources.author: Rachel Patel
sources.headline: GTM Engineer @ Deel
sources.post_summary: Walked through her framework for operationalizing content at scale: creating modular content blocks that sales reps can assemble into personalized sequences. This approach cut content creation time by 70% while maintaining message consistency across the team.

sources.author: Alex Finn
sources.headline: Founder & Solo Builder @ VibeOS | Ex-Google
sources.post_summary: Shared his 6-week journey building and launching VibeOS, a lightweight AI-native OS for indie makers. Broke down weekly progress, user feedback loops, and how he handled distribution without a marketing budget.

sources.author: Maya Torres
sources.headline: Indie Developer & Creator | Shipping in Public
sources.post_summary: Documented her pivot from marketing to full-time indie dev. Detailed the first 3 products she shipped, what failed, and how transparent weekly updates helped her gain early users and job offers.

sources.author: Ravi Patel
sources.headline: Founder at PromptLayer | Previously PM at Stripe
sources.post_summary: Wrote about rebuilding PromptLayer from scratch as a solo founder after leaving his job. Focused on the technical decisions, pricing experiments, and how he used public updates to validate demand.

sources.author: Sara Kline
sources.headline: Software Engineer | Career Switcher & Content Creator
sources.post_summary: Shared her transition from teaching to software engineering, including the projects she built publicly on LinkedIn and GitHub. Highlighted how consistent shipping helped her land her first dev role.

sources.author: Liam Chen
sources.headline: Founder @ ShipFast | Solo Developer
sources.post_summary: Posted a thread breaking down how he shipped and iterated on 4 micro-SaaS tools in 90 days. Included revenue numbers, tech stack choices, and lessons from failed launches.
